lessons: At read-only SDK boundaries, source-bound passive call wrappers can preserve native manager/object identity without deep proxying collections. Bind receiver/method before argument evaluation and verify real transaction results before adoption.
Observe metadata under protected finite bounds; never traverse mutable journals or substitute failed observation for the original call. Preserve non-returning rows rather than infer success.

Retain original permission checks and native method availability checks outside wrappers. A confirmed transfer may legitimately target another owner; source context is required when interpreting metadata.

Exact inverse and full payload/ZIP byte checks bound a private diagnostic; they do not grant game, performance or entire ownership-case success. Keep actual Core Native unknown until a fresh cold run.
